headline: High: TREK’s browser/MCP and shared file surfaces create default leakage and cascading-error risks when paired with godot_rl_agents, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the game agent’s lack of I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it is not a natural injection sink. TREK can use browsers and MCP, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or direct ingestion path. The only plausible bridge is unusual manual transfer or an external orchestrator, so the pathway exists but is weak.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies TREK output into a prompt consumed by godot_rl_agents, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted TREK output into the game agent.
Use a human review step before forwarding any TREK text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and user accounts, and it writes to ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/. godot_rl_agents has no documented data handling, but if it shares a workspace or receives TREK artifacts, leakage can occur in default TREK workflows. Uncertainty about the game agent’s storage behavior pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same filesystem path, TREK secrets or documents may be exposed to the game agent.
IF TREK logs or uploads are forwarded into godot_rl_agents prompts, sensitive content can leak into outputs.
mitigations: Place TREK and godot_rl_agents in separate containers.
Restrict access to ./data and ./uploads to TREK only.
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets.
Review TREK logs for secret material before sharing outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or shared-resource capabilities, while TREK has allowlisted egress, browser use, MCP, and collaborative real-time sessions. That means overlap is not enough to create a strong write-write conflict on the same mutable resource. The pair could conflict only if an external orchestrator gives them the same target, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator assigns both agents write access to the same database or files, conflicts become plausible.
IF TREK and the game agent are both pointed at the same MCP resource, overlapping mutations may race.
mitigations: Assign distinct resource namespaces.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Use a single writer for TREK state.
Pause one agent during critical updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and access to browsers, MCP, and external APIs, so it can act on or render upstream content. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing agent with no documented verification layer. If TREK consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative, errors can cascade into travel plans or actions. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK ingests godot_rl_agents output without verification, downstream actions may be based on false premises.
IF TREK uses AI-generated content to update reservations or documents, a bad upstream answer can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any booking or message send.
Add a verification step for all imported agent outputs.
Limit TREK to read-only mode for untrusted inputs.
Log source provenance for every AI-generated claim.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, plus local files and logs, which creates compliance obligations around retention and access control. godot_rl_agents is open-source game-playing with no data classes touched, so it is not the compliance driver. The pair risk comes from TREK’s sensitive data handling and possible residency/retention mismatch, but no specific jurisdictional breach is documented.
conditions: IF TREK stores or logs sensitive travel data longer than policy allows, retention compliance may fail.
IF TREK processes EU personal data without an appropriate transfer basis, residency compliance may fail.
mitigations: Review TREK retention settings.
Minimize logged personal data.
Restrict access to travel.db and logs.
Document data categories processed by TREK.
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows.
